title: Breath: the anchor you always carry

points.text: Of all anchors for attention, breath is the most studied and the least risky.
The only study found that compared doses directly is Fincham, Mavor and Dritschel (Mindfulness, 2023; an online dose-ranging randomised trial).
All four conditions improved, and there was no significant difference by dose.
The honest conclusion is single: the field gives no dose–response curve with a threshold of "so many minutes".
Because the list of risk factors for adverse effects includes rising intensity and retreats (review by Matko and Van Dam, Current Opinion in Psychology, 2026).
10–20 minutes, with a ceiling for all eight weeks of no more than 30–45 minutes per session. No home retreats, no days of silence, no "hundred days in a row".

outline.heading: What to do with a wandering mind

points.text: One caveat you'll need later: the breath does not need fixing.
A skipped day is not a failure.

points: Breath is the most studied and least risky anchor for your attention.
Fincham, Mavor and Dritschel found that all four conditions improved with no significant difference by dose.
The field gives no dose-response curve with a threshold of so many minutes.
Rising intensity and retreats are risk factors for adverse effects according to a review by Matko and Van Dam.
Practice for 10–20 minutes without exceeding 30–45 minutes per session or attempting home retreats, days of silence, or hundred days in a row.
You will need to remember later that the breath does not need fixing.
You have not failed if you skip a day.
